cards.title: S1-15: 7-day session cookie + revocation
cards.description:
**Description**: Sessions stored in `sessions` table with `sha256(token)`, HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite=Lax cookie, 7-day expiry. `POST /auth/logout` deletes the session row.

**Tests**: Session cookie works for 7 days. Cookie expires after 7 days and access is rejected. Logout deletes the row and the same cookie is rejected on the next request.

**Dependencies**: S1-13

cards.title: S1-16: Next.js dashboard scaffold
cards.description:
**Description**: Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript strict + Tailwind + shadcn/ui dark-mode default. Route groups for role boundaries (`(founder)`, `(pd)`, `(am)`). Server-side auth guard reading session cookie.

**Tests**: `pnpm build` succeeds with strict TypeScript. Unauthenticated access to a protected route redirects to `/login`. Dark mode is the default theme on a fresh load.

**Dependencies**: S1-04, S1-12

cards.title: S1-17: OpenAPI -> TS client codegen + TanStack Query
cards.description:
**Description**: Codegen pipeline that produces a typed TS client from `apps/api`'s OpenAPI document into `packages/shared`. TanStack Query configured with 5-10s polling defaults on active dashboard views.

**Tests**: Codegen runs cleanly in CI; generated types compile under strict mode. A sample query against `/healthz` from the dashboard renders the response without `any`.

**Dependencies**: S1-12, S1-16

cards.title: S1-18: Login + email confirmation pages
cards.description:
**Description**: `/login` page with email + password form and confirmation-flow handling. Confirmation page reads the token from the URL and calls `POST /auth/confirm/{token}`.

**Tests**: Playwright E2E: a seeded user can log in, see the empty `/clients` page, log out, and is rejected when re-using the cookie. A new user receives a confirmation email (Resend mock), clicks the link, and is logged in.

**Dependencies**: S1-14, S1-15, S1-16, S1-17

cards.title: S1-19: Inngest setup (prod + staging + local)
cards.description:
**Description**: Inngest accounts and signing keys provisioned for prod and staging. Worker process in `apps/api` registers a no-op function. Local dev uses the dev server from S1-02.

**Tests**: Sending a test event via Inngest CLI in local dev fires the registered function. Staging Inngest UI shows the worker as connected.

**Dependencies**: S1-02, S1-04

cards.title: S1-20: Sentry setup (api + dashboard, PII scrubbing)
cards.description:
**Description**: Sentry DSNs per environment. PII scrubbing rules: email, phone, transcript content, signed-PDF URLs scrubbed before send. Source maps uploaded for the dashboard.

**Tests**: A deliberate `raise` in api lands in Sentry with email scrubbed to `[Filtered]`. Dashboard runtime error lands in Sentry with a useful stack trace from source maps.

**Dependencies**: S1-04, S1-16

cards.title: S1-21: Render env groups + secret hygiene
cards.description:
**Description**: All Phase 1 secrets configured in Render env groups (per env). Pre-commit hook (already installed in S1-01) verified to scan staged files for common secret patterns.

**Tests**: Attempting to commit a file containing `sk_test_` is blocked. All staging services start with their env vars resolved (no `MISSING_ENV` errors in logs).

**Dependencies**: S1-01, S1-04

cards.title: S1-22: PandaDoc webhook receiver + HMAC verification
cards.description:
**Description**: `POST /webhooks/pandadoc` verifies HMAC signature, dedupes against `(event_type=pandadoc.signed, external_id=document.id)`, persists `onboarding_events` row, and triggers an Inngest event for downstream fan-out.

**Tests**: Valid signature + new payload creates one event row and triggers Inngest. Replay of the same payload creates no new row (idempotent). Tampered signature returns 401 and creates no row. Verified-at timestamp populated only on signature pass.

**Dependencies**: S1-08, S1-19

cards.title: S1-23: PandaDoc daily reconciliation cron
cards.description:
**Description**: Cron at 03:00 UK time pulls `documents?status=completed&signed_after=<last_check>` from PandaDoc. Any signed documents missing a corresponding `onboarding_events` row trigger a synthetic event and a Slack alert.

**Tests**: Mocked PandaDoc API returns 3 docs, 1 of which has no event row. Cron creates the missing event and posts to Slack mock. Subsequent run with no new docs is a no-op.

**Dependencies**: S1-22

cards.title: S1-24: PandaDoc manual replay endpoint
cards.description:
**Description**: `POST /admin/pandadoc/replay/{document_id}` (founder + engineer only) fetches the document via the API and emits the synthetic webhook through the same handler as S1-22.

**Tests**: Replay of a known signed document creates the event row and triggers Inngest. Replay of an unknown document returns 404. AM role gets 403.

**Dependencies**: S1-22

cards.title: S1-25: GHL sub-account creation (direct API, replaces Pabbly)
cards.description:
**Description**: Inngest function `create_ghl_subaccount` triggered by `pandadoc.signed`. Calls GHL agency API directly. Writes `platform_actions` row pre/post.

**Tests**: Mocked GHL agency API returns a sub-account id; row recorded with `status=success`, `external_id` set, `clients.ghl_subaccount_id` populated. API failure marks `status=failed` with `last_error` and increments `retry_count`. Concurrency cap of 3 enforced (verified by parallel test events).

**Dependencies**: S1-09, S1-22

cards.title: S1-26: Returning-client check + parent_client_id linking
cards.description:
**Description**: Before sub-account creation in S1-25, lookup existing GHL contact by signed-document email. If found, set `parent_client_id` on the new client row to the existing client's id and skip sub-account creation; reuse the existing `ghl_subaccount_id`.

**Tests**: First signing for an email creates a fresh client + sub-account. Second signing for the same email creates a new client row with `parent_client_id` set and reuses the existing GHL sub-account id; `platform_actions` records a `skipped_existing` outcome.

**Dependencies**: S1-25

cards.title: S1-27: Sales call transcript capture - native (Zoom + Google Meet)
cards.description:
**Description**: Webhook receivers for Zoom and Google Meet recording-completed events. Pull native transcript when available, store text in `documents` (R2 key) and trigger AI summary.

**Tests**: Zoom mock event with native transcript stores transcript in R2 and creates a `documents` row of kind `transcript_text`. Same for Google Meet. Event with no transcript falls through to S1-28 path.

**Dependencies**: S1-10, S1-19, plus R2 buckets created (covered by S1-21 env groups)

cards.title: S1-28: Sales call transcript fallback - OpenAI Whisper
cards.description:
**Description**: When native transcript is missing, download recording audio, send to Whisper API, store text in R2, write `documents` row of kind `transcript_text`. Soft cost cap $50/mo with alert at 80%.

**Tests**: Mocked recording with no native transcript triggers Whisper path; `documents` row created. Cost-tracker accumulator emits an alert at 80% of cap.

**Dependencies**: S1-27

cards.title: S1-29: AI sales summary generator
cards.description:
**Description**: Inngest function `summarise_sales_call`. Anthropic SDK call with `claude-opus-4-7`, prompt caching enabled (system prompt + few-shot examples cached, transcript not cached). Output validated against the Pydantic schema in PRD section 7.1.

**Tests**: Given a fixture transcript, the function produces JSON matching the schema. Prompt-cache hit observed on the second call within 5 minutes (verified via response metadata). Schema-invalid output fails the function and surfaces in `platform_actions` with a clear `last_error`.

**Dependencies**: S1-27 (transcript present)

cards.title: S1-30: Write summary to client_knowledge with embeddings
cards.description:
**Description**: For each top-level field of the sales summary, insert one row into `client_knowledge` with `source=sales_call`. Compute embedding for `value_text` and store in `embedding` column.

**Tests**: A summary with 7 fields produces 7 `client_knowledge` rows. Each row has a non-null embedding. Re-running the summariser for the same client + transcript does not duplicate rows (idempotent on `(client_id, source, key, captured_at)`).

**Dependencies**: S1-07, S1-29

cards.title: S1-31: Dashboard /clients list view
cards.description:
**Description**: Server-rendered table of every client with current_step, time-in-step, last platform action status, and a link to the detail page. 10s polling.

**Tests**: Playwright: with 3 seeded clients in different steps, the list renders all 3 with correct steps. Polling fetches a fresh row when a fourth client is inserted server-side.

**Dependencies**: S1-06, S1-17, S1-18

cards.title: S1-32: Dashboard /clients/[id] detail view (Sprint 1 slice)
cards.description:
**Description**: Detail page shows client metadata, current_step, AI sales summary (if present), platform deep-links (placeholders for platforms not yet integrated). 5s polling on active fields.

**Tests**: Playwright: opening a seeded client with a sales summary renders the structured summary fields. Opening a client without a summary shows a clear "no summary yet" state. Inngest run id deep-link opens the Inngest UI for a recorded action.

**Dependencies**: S1-30, S1-31

cards.title: S1-33: GitHub Actions CI
cards.description:
**Description**: PR workflow runs lint (`ruff` + `eslint`), typecheck (`mypy` + `tsc --noEmit`), and tests (`pytest` + `vitest` + Playwright). Per-PR Neon branch is created and torn down.

**Tests**: A PR introducing a lint error fails CI. A PR adding a passing test passes CI. Per-PR Neon branch is visible in the Neon dashboard during the run and removed after merge/close.

**Dependencies**: S1-01, S1-03

cards.title: S1-34: Auto-deploy to Render staging on merge to main
cards.description:
**Description**: Render auto-deploy hook on push to `main`. Promotion to production is manual via the Render dashboard.

**Tests**: A merge to `main` deploys all four staging services. The production services do not auto-deploy (verified by inspecting Render deploy logs).

**Dependencies**: S1-04, S1-33

cards.title: S1-35: Sprint 1 acceptance verification
cards.description:
**Description**: Walk through every PRD section 12.1 acceptance criterion against the staging environment with the Bullet team. Any failure resets the sprint sign-off.

**Tests**: Acceptance log committed at `docs/sprint-1-acceptance.md` with each criterion ticked, evidence linked, and any deferred items recorded with rationale.

**Dependencies**: S1-22, S1-23, S1-25, S1-26, S1-29, S1-31, S1-32, S1-34

cards.title: S2-01: Slack incoming webhook integration
cards.description:
**Description**: Adapter sending one-way notifications to `#bullet_inbound_clients` (and other channels via env config). New-signing notification includes deep links to dashboard, HubSpot, GHL, Drive, Asana, Calendar.

**Tests**: Mocked Slack endpoint receives a well-formed message with all expected deep links on a `pandadoc.signed` event. Backoff retries on 429 (1 msg/sec rate limit) verified.

**Dependencies**: S1-22

cards.title: S2-02: Asana integration - project + finance task + onboarding subtasks
cards.description:
**Description**: Inngest function creates `Bullet Clients Status` project, finance task, onboarding subtasks per service-tier template. Stores `asana_project_id` and `asana_finance_task_id` on the client.

**Tests**: Mocked Asana API call creates the expected hierarchy. Idempotency key prevents duplicate project on retry. Concurrency cap 5 enforced.

**Dependencies**: S1-09, S1-22

cards.title: S2-03: Asana template checksum monitoring
cards.description:
**Description**: Daily cron pulls each tracked Asana template, hashes the structure, and alerts Slack on drift.

**Tests**: Mocked template change triggers an alert; unchanged template does not. Template registry stored in DB.

**Dependencies**: S2-01, S2-02

cards.title: S2-04: Google Sheets - client row creation
cards.description:
**Description**: Adapter writes a row in the `Client Status Sheet` matching today's schema, including the `SaaS Mode` passthrough column. Stores `sheet_row_id` on the client.

**Tests**: Mocked Sheets API call creates a row with all current columns. Re-run for the same client updates the existing row, does not create a duplicate.

**Dependencies**: S1-09, S1-22

cards.title: S2-05: Google Drive - folder tree creation + sharing
cards.description:
**Description**: Creates the actively-used folder tree per client (legacy folders skipped pending plan section 11 Q-2). Applies sharing per service-account configuration. Stores `drive_folder_id` on the client.

**Tests**: Mocked Drive API creates the expected folder structure. Sharing permissions match the configured spec. Idempotent on retry (returns existing folder id).

**Dependencies**: S1-09, S1-22

cards.title: S2-06: Google Calendar - kick-off booking + change subscription
cards.description:
**Description**: Books the kick-off call via the existing GHL calendar link. Subscribes to calendar-change events; date changes propagate to Asana finance task in S3-13 (groundwork now).

**Tests**: Mocked Calendar API creates the booking and stores the event id. A simulated calendar webhook for a date change is received and persisted as an `onboarding_events` row of type `calendar.kickoff_changed`.

**Dependencies**: S1-09, S1-22

cards.title: S2-07: HubSpot integration - contact read + stage mirror
cards.description:
**Description**: Read contact fields used at PandaDoc template creation time. Mirror onboarding stage transitions back to HubSpot deal (optional but cheap to add now).

**Tests**: Mocked HubSpot API returns contact data; client row populated with contact fields. Stage transition updates the deal stage; failure does not block the fan-out (writes a `failed` `platform_actions` row but the rest proceeds).

**Dependencies**: S1-09, S1-22

cards.title: S2-08: Inngest fan-out workflow + per-platform concurrency
cards.description:
**Description**: Single Inngest workflow function fans out to S2-01 through S2-07 in parallel with per-platform concurrency caps from PRD section 6.3.

**Tests**: A `pandadoc.signed` event triggers all six fan-out actions and they execute concurrently subject to the caps. A burst of 20 simulated signings respects the per-platform caps (verified via Inngest run logs).

**Dependencies**: S2-01, S2-02, S2-04, S2-05, S2-06, S2-07

cards.title: S2-09: Idempotency + retry policy enforcement
cards.description:
**Description**: Every fan-out function obeys the PRD section 6.1 - 6.4 rules: idempotency_key, exponential backoff (1m, 5m, 15m, 1h, 6h), max 5 attempts, dead-letter on final failure.

**Tests**: A function that fails 4 times then succeeds records 5 attempts and final `status=success`. A function that fails 5 times records `status=dead_lettered`. Slack escalation alert fires on attempt 3.

**Dependencies**: S2-08

cards.title: S2-10: Dashboard /actions cross-client action health
cards.description:
**Description**: View showing all `platform_actions` filtered by status (failed, retrying, dead-lettered). Per-row Inngest deep-link. 10s polling.

**Tests**: Playwright: a seeded set of actions in mixed states renders correctly. Filter controls update the list. Inngest deep-link opens the correct run page.

**Dependencies**: S1-31, S2-09

cards.title: S2-11: Manual retry button (dead-letter recovery)
cards.description:
**Description**: Per-action retry button on `/actions` (founder + PD only). Re-enqueues the action via Inngest with a fresh attempt counter.

**Tests**: Clicking retry on a dead-lettered action enqueues an Inngest event; on success the row flips to `status=success`. AM role does not see the button.

**Dependencies**: S2-10

cards.title: S2-12: GHL OB V2 portal completion webhook
cards.description:
**Description**: `POST /webhooks/ghl/portal` verifies signature, dedupes on `(event_type=ghl.portal_completed, external_id=response.id)`, persists `onboarding_events`.

**Tests**: Valid event creates one row; replay creates none. Tampered signature rejected.

**Dependencies**: S1-08, S1-19

cards.title: S2-13: Portal data ingestion to client_knowledge
cards.description:
**Description**: Inngest function transforms the GHL portal payload into structured `client_knowledge` rows with `source=portal` and computed embeddings.

**Tests**: Sample portal payload produces the expected set of knowledge rows. Re-running for the same response id is idempotent.

**Dependencies**: S1-30, S2-12

cards.title: S2-14: campaign_flow_type field + PD selection UI
cards.description:
**Description**: PD picks `low_ticket_checkout` or `high_ticket_consultation` on the client detail page. Default suggestion inferred from portal answers (`group_size=small AND consultation_price>0` -> high-ticket; else low-ticket). Audit-logged.

**Tests**: PD can select a value; AM cannot. Default suggestion populates from portal data. Selection writes to `clients.campaign_flow_type` and an `audit_log` row.

**Dependencies**: S1-32, S2-13

cards.title: S2-15: Pricing calculator - subscription anchor
cards.description:
**Description**: Pure function: `anchor_value = monthly_price / 30.4 * offer_days`. Returns the worked breakdown alongside the result.

**Tests**: `£200 / 30.4 * 21` returns `£138.16` to two decimal places. Edge cases: zero offer_days returns 0; negative inputs raise. Worked-string contains the inputs and result.

**Dependencies**: n/a

cards.title: S2-16: Pricing calculator - class-pack anchor
cards.description:
**Description**: Pure function: `anchor_value = drop_in_rate * class_count`.

**Tests**: `£30 * 5 = £150.00`. Worked-string format matches the subscription anchor's contract for consistent dashboard rendering.

**Dependencies**: n/a

cards.title: S2-17: Kick-off transcript capture
cards.description:
**Description**: Mirror of S1-27 + S1-28 for kick-off calls. Triggers AI follow-up email generation.

**Tests**: Kick-off recording event captures transcript via native or Whisper. `documents` row created with kind `transcript_text`. Triggers the appropriate variant generator.

**Dependencies**: S1-27, S1-28

cards.title: S2-18: Kick-off email generator - low-ticket variant
cards.description:
**Description**: Anthropic call with kick-off transcript + portal answers + sales summary + brand assets + historical-offers corpus. Combines S2-15 / S2-16 outputs. Produces JSON per PRD section 7.2 plus calculation transparency string.

**Tests**: Fixture inputs produce JSON validating against the schema. `total_value`, `savings`, `percent_off` computed correctly. Three offer-name suggestions returned. Calculation transparency string includes every input and the final result.

**Dependencies**: S2-15, S2-16, S2-17, S1-30

cards.title: S2-19: Kick-off email generator - high-ticket variant
cards.description:
**Description**: Anthropic call producing JSON per PRD section 7.3 (prose-only, no maths block).

**Tests**: Fixture inputs produce schema-valid JSON. No `total_value` / `savings` / `percent_off` fields present. `email_body` references the agreed offer structure, ad budget, start date, creative requirements, kickoff date.

**Dependencies**: S2-17, S1-30

cards.title: S2-20: Dashboard - Ready for PD Review state
cards.description:
**Description**: Client detail surfaces the AI draft, suggested offer names (low-ticket only), worked pricing or prose, with edit controls. Status badge `Ready for PD Review`.

**Tests**: Playwright: a client with a generated low-ticket draft renders all three offer-name suggestions and the worked maths. PD edits the email body and the change persists. AM cannot edit, only view.

**Dependencies**: S1-32, S2-18, S2-19

cards.title: S2-21: PD confirm action -> Ready for AM to Send
cards.description:
**Description**: PD clicks Confirm; status transitions; an `audit_log` row is written with the before/after values.

**Tests**: Confirm transitions the client to `Ready for AM to Send`. AM role does not see the Confirm button. Audit-log row captured.

**Dependencies**: S2-20

cards.title: S2-22: AM Send action -> Resend dispatch
cards.description:
**Description**: AM clicks Send; Resend API call with the confirmed email body. `documents` row of kind `kickoff_followup_email_body` created. `platform_actions` records the send.

**Tests**: Mocked Resend send returns success; client transitions to `Sent`; document row created. Send failure surfaces in `/actions`. Idempotency key prevents double-send on a click stutter.

**Dependencies**: S2-21

notes.content: Q-01 resolved 06/05/2026: Bullet confirmed single system mailbox via Resend (e.g. onboarding@bulletdigitalmedia.com) for all system-originated client emails (kick-off follow-up, technical-requirements replacement, auth confirmation, dashboard alerts). Replies route via a catch-all rule into a shared Bullet inbox; per-message reply-to header preserves thread context where useful. No per-AM Gmail-API delegated-send work needed. This card and the Sprint 2 email cluster (S2-23, S2-24, S2-25) plus Sprint 3 tech-requirements cards (S3-10, S3-11) are now locked to Resend. See docs/openquestions.md Resolved and docs/CHANGELOG.md entry for 06/05/2026.
notes.author: claude

cards.title: S2-23: Resend domain setup (SPF / DKIM / DMARC)
cards.description:
**Description**: Configure DNS records on `bulletdigitalmedia.com` for Resend. Verify status in Resend dashboard.

**Tests**: Resend dashboard reports all three records as verified. A test send to a Gmail address arrives without spam-folder routing and passes SPF/DKIM/DMARC checks (verified in raw headers).

**Dependencies**: n/a (DNS is owned by Bullet; coordinate via Chris)

cards.title: S2-24: React Email templates
cards.description:
**Description**: React Email components for: auth confirmation (S1-14), kick-off follow-up email (both variants), tech-requirements email (Sprint 3), dashboard alerts.

**Tests**: Each template renders to HTML and to plain-text fallback. Snapshot tests pin the rendered output. Variables interpolated correctly in fixtures.

**Dependencies**: S2-23

cards.title: S2-25: Resend reply handling + bounce/complaint webhook
cards.description:
**Description**: `POST /webhooks/resend` records bounces and complaints into `audit_log`. Reply routing rule lands replies in the configured shared inbox.

**Tests**: Mocked bounce webhook creates an audit_log row. Complaint webhook same. Manual test send + reply lands in the configured inbox.

**Dependencies**: S2-22, S2-23

cards.title: S2-26: End-to-end happy path test
cards.description:
**Description**: Playwright + API integration test that simulates a PandaDoc signing event and asserts every Sprint 1 + Sprint 2 fan-out completes successfully without human intervention. Asserts the kick-off email path through PD review -> AM send.

**Tests**: A scripted run from `pandadoc.signed` to `Sent` produces a green run with all expected `platform_actions` rows in `success` and the dashboard reflecting the final state.

**Dependencies**: S2-08, S2-22

cards.title: S2-27: MVP demo to Bullet team
cards.description:
**Description**: Live walkthrough on staging. Validate against a simulated onboarding flow with the Bullet team observing. Capture feedback into `docs/dashboard-feedback/client-feedback-log.md`.

**Tests**: Demo checklist signed off by John or Stephen; feedback log updated; any P0 issues converted into Sprint 3 tasks before sprint sign-off.

**Dependencies**: S2-26

cards.title: S3-01: Stripe customer creation + UK / International routing
cards.description:
**Description**: Inngest function creates a Stripe customer on the appropriate account (UK or International) based on `clients.legal_entity`. Stores `stripe_customer_id`.

**Tests**: Mocked Stripe API: UK client creates customer on UK account; International on the other. Idempotency key prevents duplicate creation.

**Dependencies**: S2-08

cards.title: S3-02: Stripe payment_method.attached webhook
cards.description:
**Description**: `POST /webhooks/stripe` verifies signature, persists `payment_method.attached`, attaches the method to the customer.

**Tests**: Valid webhook with signature attaches PM; tampered signature rejected; replay is idempotent.

**Dependencies**: S3-01

cards.title: S3-03: Stripe deferred subscription activation
cards.description:
**Description**: Subscription created only after the kick-off follow-up email is sent (S2-22). Inngest function listens for `client.kickoff_email_sent` event and creates the subscription with native Stripe idempotency.

**Tests**: Subscription created exactly once per client. Premature trigger (before send) does not create one. Failure surfaces in `/actions`.

**Dependencies**: S2-22, S3-02

cards.title: S3-04: Stripe Amex flagging in dashboard
cards.description:
**Description**: Detect Amex payment method via Stripe webhook brand field. Surface a distinct Amex flag on the client detail page; pipeline does not stall on missing PM for Amex clients.

**Tests**: Amex test PM triggers the flag; Visa does not. Pipeline continues for an Amex client without a captured PM (subscription activation deferred to manual capture, recorded in audit log).

**Dependencies**: S3-02

cards.title: S3-05: Xero OAuth setup + token refresh
cards.description:
**Description**: OAuth 2.0 flow with offline access. Tokens stored encrypted in env-protected DB rows; refresh handled automatically.

**Tests**: Initial OAuth handshake succeeds (manual). Refresh token swap after expiry succeeds without manual intervention. Token-revocation case logs cleanly and alerts Slack.

**Dependencies**: n/a

cards.title: S3-06: Xero contact creation with chart-of-accounts + tracking categories
cards.description:
**Description**: Inngest function creates a Xero contact with the appropriate chart-of-accounts and tracking categories per `legal_entity`. Stores `xero_contact_id`.

**Tests**: Mocked Xero API: UK and International route to different chart-of-accounts (exact rule pending plan Q-3). Idempotent. Rate limit (60 req/min) backoff verified.

**Dependencies**: S3-05, S2-08

cards.title: S3-07: Timely client + project creation
cards.description:
**Description**: Inngest function creates a Timely client and project; project budget = `monthly_fee_usd / 100` hours. Stores `timely_client_id` and `timely_project_id`. Team assignment remains a dashboard-driven action.

**Tests**: Mocked Timely API: client and project created with the correct budget. Idempotent. Concurrency cap 3 enforced.

**Dependencies**: S2-08

cards.title: S3-08: client_assets population per client
cards.description:
**Description**: On `pandadoc.signed`, populate `client_assets` rows from a configurable per-service-tier template (e.g. `ad_account_access`, `regulatory_docs`, `headshot`, `brand_guidelines`, `face_to_camera_video`, `logo_files`, etc.).

**Tests**: A signed agreement for a known service tier creates the expected set of `client_assets` rows in `status=required`. Idempotent on replay.

**Dependencies**: S2-08

cards.title: S3-09: Dashboard asset checklist UI
cards.description:
**Description**: Per-client live checklist: asset type, status, requested at, source url. Actions: mark received, mark approved, mark waived, send chase email.

**Tests**: Playwright: PD or AM can mark received; status flips; audit-log row written. Mark waived requires a note (enforced).

**Dependencies**: S3-08, S1-32

cards.title: S3-10: Single conditional asset-chase email template
cards.description:
**Description**: One React Email template with conditional blocks for each outstanding asset type. Replaces the 16-branch GHL Outstanding Elements workflow entirely.

**Tests**: Snapshot tests for representative asset combinations (e.g. only headshot missing; ad account + regulatory docs missing; everything required). Manual send to a test inbox renders correctly.

**Dependencies**: S2-24

cards.title: S3-11: Send chase email action wired to template
cards.description:
**Description**: "Send chase email" button on the asset checklist composes the conditional email from current `client_assets` state and sends via Resend.

**Tests**: A client with two outstanding assets receives an email referencing exactly those two. `platform_actions` records the send. Idempotency window of 30 minutes prevents accidental double-chase.

**Dependencies**: S3-09, S3-10

cards.title: S3-12: Preserve existing GHL conditional workflows
cards.description:
**Description**: Continue triggering existing GHL workflows where they remain (post-signing portal link, survey reminders). No rebuild; just ensure the trigger fires.

**Tests**: A `pandadoc.signed` event still triggers the post-signing portal link workflow in GHL (verified via GHL workflow logs in staging). Survey-reminder cadence unchanged.

**Dependencies**: S2-08

cards.title: S3-13: Calendar -> Asana date propagation
cards.description:
**Description**: Calendar-change webhook (S2-06) updates the Asana finance task due date idempotently. Eliminates Steve's Monday manual sync.

**Tests**: Simulated calendar reschedule for a known client updates the Asana finance task date. Re-running the same change is a no-op. Failure surfaces in `/actions`.

**Dependencies**: S2-02, S2-06

cards.title: S3-14: Sprint 3 acceptance verification
cards.description:
**Description**: Walk through every PRD section 12.3 acceptance criterion against staging with the Bullet team.

**Tests**: Acceptance log committed at `docs/sprint-3-acceptance.md` with each criterion ticked and evidence linked.

**Dependencies**: S3-01, S3-03, S3-04, S3-06, S3-07, S3-09, S3-10, S3-11, S3-12, S3-13

cards.title: S4-01: Firecrawl integration - client website scrape
cards.description:

cards.title: S1-14: Resend email confirmation flow
cards.description:
**Description**: New users receive a confirmation email via Resend with a 24h-expiring token. `email_confirmed=false` blocks login. `POST /auth/confirm/{token}` flips the flag and timestamps `email_confirmed_at`.

**Tests**: Unconfirmed user cannot log in (403 with a clear message). Confirmation link within 24h flips the flag. Expired token returns 410. Resend API client is mockable in tests.

**Dependencies**: S1-13

notes.content:
🤖 Task Completed

**What was implemented**:
- `apps/api/pyproject.toml` — added `itsdangerous>=2.2,<3.0` (signed time-limited tokens, no users-table migration needed) and pinned `httpx>=0.27,<1.0` for the Resend REST client.
- `apps/api/src/bullet_api/config.py` — four new settings: `email_token_secret` (signing key, defaults to `dev-insecure-change-me` so a missed Render env-group override is obvious), `resend_api_key` (defaults empty; client refuses to send when blank), `email_from` (`onboarding@bulletdigitalmedia.com` per Q-01 06/05/2026), `email_confirmation_base_url`.
- `apps/api/src/bullet_api/email/__init__.py` + `client.py` (new):
  - `EmailClient` Protocol — handlers depend on the interface, not Resend specifically.
  - `EmailMessage` frozen dataclass (`to, subject, html, from_email`).
  - `ResendEmailClient` — posts to `https://api.resend.com/emails` with httpx; raises `RuntimeError` if `api_key` is empty so a misconfigured deploy fails loudly rather than silently dropping mail.
  - `FakeEmailClient` — captures every sent `EmailMessage` on `.sent` for assertions.
  - `get_email_client` FastAPI dependency that tests override.
- `apps/api/src/bullet_api/auth/confirmation.py` (new):
  - `generate_confirmation_token(user_id)` and `_decode_confirmation_token(token)` using `itsdangerous.URLSafeTimedSerializer` with salt `bullet-email-confirmation-v1` and 24-hour `max_age` enforced at verification time.
  - `send_confirmation_email(user_id, email, email_client)` — builds the dashboard link (`<base>/{token}`), HTML body with a 24h note, and hands an `EmailMessage` to the injected client.
  - `POST /auth/confirm/{token}` — flips `email_confirmed=true` + stamps `email_confirmed_at=now()`. Idempotent: re-click on an already-confirmed user returns `{status:"already_confirmed"}` (200). Expired token → 410 with "Confirmation link expired" detail. Bad signature or unknown user → 400 with a generic "Invalid confirmation token" so the endpoint doesn't leak existence.
  - `POST /auth/resend-confirmation` with body `{email}` — always returns 200 with `{status:"sent_if_unconfirmed"}` regardless of whether the email matched a real user or whether that user was already confirmed. Prevents the endpoint from being a free user-enumeration oracle. Only actually sends when the email matched an unconfirmed user.
- `apps/api/src/bullet_api/auth/__init__.py` re-exports `confirmation_router`, `generate_confirmation_token`, `send_confirmation_email`.
- `apps/api/src/bullet_api/main.py` — `app.include_router(confirmation_router)`.
- `apps/api/tests/test_confirmation.py` (new) — 8 `@pytest.mark.db` tests using `FakeEmailClient` via `app.dependency_overrides[get_email_client]`.

**Verification (all green, 18/05/2026, against Neon staging)**:
- `pytest tests/test_confirmation.py -v` — 8 passed in 54.92s.
- `pytest -v` (full api suite) — **64 passed in 329.78s**. Includes every preceding Sprint 1 contract test.
- `ruff check src tests alembic` — clean.
- Independent code-review pass via the `compound-engineering:review:ce-correctness-reviewer` sub-agent — no genuine bugs found; the reviewer traced the lockout state machine, argon2 verify error funnel, itsdangerous round-trip, user-enumeration mitigation on `/auth/resend-confirmation`, libpq query-param stripping, and `X-Forwarded-For` parser. All assertions in `test_auth_dependencies`, `test_login`, and `test_confirmation` were confirmed to actually exercise the contract their names claim.

**Test contract from the card**:
- ✅ Unconfirmed user cannot log in (403 with a clear message). Already covered by `test_unconfirmed_email_returns_403` in S1-13's suite.
- ✅ Confirmation link within 24h flips the flag (`test_confirm_within_24h_flips_email_confirmed`).
- ✅ Expired token returns 410 (`test_expired_token_returns_410`, simulates 25h-old token via `time.time` monkey-patch when generating).
- ✅ Resend API client is mockable in tests (`FakeEmailClient`, `test_resend_confirmation_sends_via_email_client`, `test_send_confirmation_email_uses_injected_client`).

**Decisions**:
- Stateless signed tokens via itsdangerous over a DB-stored token. Avoided a users-table migration; rotating `EMAIL_TOKEN_SECRET` or the `_TOKEN_SALT` constant invalidates every outstanding token without touching DB rows.
- `/auth/resend-confirmation` returns the same response shape for hit, miss, and already-confirmed cases. Closing the existence-oracle path is cheap and worth it.
- `ResendEmailClient` fails loudly on empty API key rather than no-op'ing. Mis-configured Render env groups surface at first send attempt, not after a customer didn't get an email.

**Residual risks (from reviewer, not blocking)**:
- `_default_tracker` singleton lives module-scope; a future test that forgets to override `get_tracker` could see stale failures from a previous test run. Documented.
- `Secure` cookie is unconditional in S1-13; local-dev login through a browser won't persist the cookie over HTTP. Acceptable for the staging-first workflow; a `BULLET_DEV_INSECURE=1` toggle can be added later if pure local-dev becomes a real path.
- `X-Forwarded-For` is trusted unconditionally — fine on Render (front-proxy overwrites), but flag this before any topology change that exposes the API without a trusted proxy in front.
- `POST /auth/resend-confirmation` body is a plain `dict[str, str]`; a non-string value would 500 instead of 422. Minor, low-impact; switch to a Pydantic `ResendRequest` if/when more fields land.

**Status**: Ready for user review and approval.
**Moved from**: In Progress → To Review

cards.title: S1-13: Username/password auth + argon2id
cards.description:
**Description**: `POST /auth/login` accepts email + password, verifies under argon2id, issues a session cookie. Brute-force protection: 5 failed attempts in 15 minutes from the same IP triggers a 15-minute lockout.

**Tests**: Valid credentials issue a session cookie. Invalid credentials return 401. Five rapid failures from the same IP trigger lockout; sixth attempt returns 429 even with valid credentials. Lockout expires after 15 minutes.

**Dependencies**: S1-11, S1-12

notes.content:
🤖 Task Completed

**What was implemented**:
- `apps/api/src/bullet_api/auth/brute_force.py` (new):
  - `BruteForceTracker` sliding-window per-IP failure counter. Defaults: 5 attempts in 15 min triggers a 15-min lockout.
  - `clock` is injectable via constructor so tests can simulate the window elapsing.
  - Thread-safe (uses `threading.Lock`).
  - `get_tracker()` FastAPI dependency exposes a module-level singleton; tests override it to swap in a per-test instance.
- `apps/api/src/bullet_api/auth/login.py` (new):
  - `POST /auth/login` with `LoginRequest(email: EmailStr, password: str)`.
  - Order: lockout check → email lookup → argon2id verify → email_confirmed check → session mint. Lockout-first prevents email-validity timing oracles.
  - Argon2id verify uses `argon2.PasswordHasher.verify()`. Failures (`VerifyMismatchError`, `VerificationError`, `InvalidHash`) record a brute-force failure and return 401.
  - Session token: `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`; stored as `sha256(token)` in `sessions.token_hash` (matches PRD §4.9). `expires_at = now() + 7 days`. `ip` and `user_agent` also captured.
  - `users.last_login_at` updated on successful login.
  - Cookie set with `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Max-Age=604800` (7 days).
  - `X-Forwarded-For` honoured for caller-IP detection so Render's front-proxy reports the real client.
- `apps/api/src/bullet_api/auth/__init__.py` updated to re-export `login_router`.
- `apps/api/src/bullet_api/main.py` — `app.include_router(login_router)`.
- `apps/api/pyproject.toml` — added `email-validator>=2.2,<3.0` (required by pydantic `EmailStr`).
- `apps/api/tests/conftest.py` — `async_session` now binds to an outer transaction with `join_transaction_mode="create_savepoint"` so any `commit()` inside a handler under test is contained within a savepoint and rolled back at teardown. This is what makes it safe to test commit-issuing handlers against live Neon.
- `apps/api/tests/test_login.py` (new) — 7 `@pytest.mark.db` tests.

**Verification (all green, 18/05/2026, against Neon staging)**:
- `pytest tests/test_login.py -v` — 7 passed in 61.30s:
  - ✅ `test_valid_credentials_issue_session_cookie` — Set-Cookie carries HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite=Lax, a fresh `sessions` row exists, status=ok.
  - ✅ `test_invalid_password_returns_401`.
  - ✅ `test_unknown_email_returns_401`.
  - ✅ `test_unconfirmed_email_returns_403` (sets the contract that S1-14 will land on the user side).
  - ✅ `test_five_failures_lock_out_sixth_attempt_with_valid_creds` — 5 wrong-password posts, then 6th with the *correct* password from the same IP returns 429.
  - ✅ `test_lockout_expires_after_15_minutes` — clock is advanced 16 minutes via the injected lambda; 7th attempt then succeeds.
  - ✅ `test_lockout_is_per_ip` — same email from a different `X-Forwarded-For` IP is not locked out.
- `ruff check src tests alembic` — clean after auto-fix of import ordering.

**Decisions**:
- In-memory brute-force tracker. Render starter plan = single replica; restarts only on deploy. Real distributed lockout (Redis or Postgres) ships when the API scales out in S2+. The file is the swap point.
- Lockout-first ordering. A locked-out attacker timing requests should not be able to discover whether an email exists. The 429 returns before any DB lookup.
- Savepoint-wrapped test sessions (conftest change). Lets us test commit-issuing handlers against live Neon without leaving residual data. Pattern is reusable for S1-14 and later sprints (S1-22 PandaDoc webhook, S1-25 GHL sub-account, etc.).
- `email_confirmed=false` returns 403 with a "please complete the confirmation link" message. The user has valid creds; this is informational, not an auth failure. Importantly: a 403-confirmed-email is NOT counted as a brute-force failure - the lockout exists to slow password-guessing, not to penalise valid users whose confirmation step is pending.
- `Secure` cookie attribute is always set, including for the local dev server. This means the cookie won't be sent over plain HTTP at all - acceptable because local dev should run behind `make api-dev` which is HTTP-only and won't accept a Secure cookie; the dashboard's full flow is exercised against staging via HTTPS. If pure local dev needs the cookie, set `BULLET_DEV_INSECURE=1` (future) to relax. Not adding the toggle yet.

**Status**: Ready for user review and approval.
**Moved from**: In Progress → To Review

cards.description:

notes.content:
🤖 Task Completed

**What was implemented**:
- `apps/api/src/bullet_api/logging_config.py` (new) — `JsonFormatter` + `configure_logging()`. Stdlib-only JSON formatter so every record (FastAPI, uvicorn, asyncpg, sqlalchemy, our own modules) emits a single line of structured JSON that Render's log viewer can field-search. Idempotent — re-imports don't stack handlers.
- `apps/api/src/bullet_api/auth/__init__.py` + `apps/api/src/bullet_api/auth/dependencies.py` (new) — core auth primitives:
  - `CurrentUser` frozen dataclass (`id, email, full_name, role`).
  - `get_current_user` — reads the `session` cookie, sha256 hashes it (matches PRD §4.9 / S1-15 spec: `sessions.token_hash` stores the hash, never the raw token), joins `sessions` → `users` with `expires_at > now()`. Returns 401 on missing cookie, expired session, or unknown token.
  - `require_role(*allowed_roles)` factory — wraps `Depends(get_current_user)` and 403s when `user.role` is not in `allowed_roles`. The inner function's `__name__` is set so FastAPI debug output is readable.
  - Four named gates: `require_founder`, `require_pd`, `require_am`, `require_engineer` matching the four `user_role` enum values.
- `apps/api/src/bullet_api/main.py` (rewritten) — installs JSON logging on import; declares `/healthz` (unchanged), `/version`, `/me` (behind `get_current_user`), `/admin/ping` (behind `require_founder`). FastAPI's default OpenAPI 3.1 emission preserved.
- `apps/api/tests/test_auth_dependencies.py` (new) — 9 tests using `httpx.AsyncClient` + `ASGITransport` instead of `fastapi.testclient.TestClient`.

**Verification (all green, 18/05/2026, against Neon staging)**:
- `pytest tests/test_auth_dependencies.py -v` — 9 passed in 35.23s:
  - ✅ `/healthz` still 200 (regression guard).
  - ✅ `/version` returns a non-empty string.
  - ✅ `/admin/ping` 200 for founder cookie.
  - ✅ `/admin/ping` 403 for account_manager cookie.
  - ✅ `/admin/ping` 401 without any cookie.
  - ✅ `/admin/ping` 401 for unknown cookie value.
  - ✅ `/admin/ping` 401 for an expired session (with a defensive in-test assertion that the seeded row really is expired, guarding against clock skew with Neon).
  - ✅ `/me` returns id + role for `performance_director` cookie.
  - ✅ `/openapi.json` validates: `openapi 3.1.x`, `info.title=bullet-api`, all four paths present.
- `ruff check src tests alembic` — clean.

**Decisions**:
- `httpx.AsyncClient` + `ASGITransport` over `fastapi.testclient.TestClient` for any test that shares an `AsyncSession` with the request handler. TestClient runs the ASGI app on a separate anyio thread, which is incompatible with an asyncpg connection bound to the pytest event loop.
- `Annotated[..., Depends(get_session)]` over the older `dep: T = Depends(...)` form so ruff's B008 ("function call in default") doesn't fire.
- Endpoints `/me` and `/admin/ping` ship now rather than being purely test scaffolding. `/me` is what the dashboard polls on bootstrap; `/admin/ping` is a cheap dependency-graph smoke test for ops.
- JSON logging is stdlib-only (no `python-json-logger` / `structlog` dep). Twelve lines of formatter code; nothing fancy. Easy to extend with request-id / trace-id correlation when needed.

**Status**: Ready for user review and approval.

notes.content:
🤖 Task Completed

**What was implemented**:
- `apps/api/alembic/versions/0005_create_platform_actions.py` — migration per PRD §4.4.
  - Two postgresql ENUMs:
    - `platform_action_platform` — 16 values (`hubspot`, `pandadoc`, `ghl`, `asana`, `stripe`, `xero`, `timely`, `slack`, `gsheets`, `gdocs`, `gdrive`, `gmail`, `gcal`, `meta`, `resend`, `firecrawl`).

  - `event_id` nullable FK to onboarding_events with `ON DELETE SET NULL` — synthetic/reconciliation actions can exist without an event, and we never want to lose the audit row if an event is later cleaned up.
  - `idempotency_key text NOT NULL UNIQUE` — the workhorse contract. Pattern: `{client_id}:{platform}:{action}:{event_id}`. Writer code will `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING RETURNING *` and re-fetch on conflict to resume an in-flight action. UNIQUE auto-creates a btree index, so no manual `op.create_index` for it.
  - `retry_count int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` — server-side default so Inngest-side retry bookkeeping has a clean baseline.
  - Other columns: `payload`, `response`, `external_id`, `last_error`, `inngest_run_id`, `started_at`, `completed_at` per PRD §4.4.
  - Indexes: `client_id`, `(client_id, platform, action)` composite, `status`, `started_at DESC` (functional descending index).
- `apps/api/tests/test_platform_actions_table.py` (new) — 4 `@pytest.mark.db` tests.

**Verification (all green, 18/05/2026, against Neon staging)**:
- `alembic upgrade head` (0004 → 0005) — clean.
- `pytest tests/test_platform_actions_table.py -v` — 4 passed in 25.87s:
  - ✅ `test_insert_pending_action_succeeds` — confirms `retry_count` defaults to 0, status persists as `'pending'`.
  - ✅ `test_duplicate_idempotency_key_is_rejected` — second insert with same `idempotency_key` raises `IntegrityError`. This is the guarantee that the orchestrator can replay an Inngest run safely.
  - ✅ `test_status_transitions_through_lifecycle` — `pending → in_progress → success` UPDATE chain works without constraint violation; `started_at` populated via `COALESCE(started_at, now())` pattern.
  - ✅ `test_invalid_platform_enum_is_rejected` — Postgres rejects `'NOT_A_PLATFORM'`.

**Decisions**:
- `idempotency_key` is unconstrained `TEXT` rather than e.g. checking the `{a}:{b}:{c}:{d}` shape at the DB level. The shape is a code-level convention; enforcing it in SQL would couple the schema to the writer implementation and slow future iterations.
- `retry_count` is `INTEGER` not `SMALLINT` — gives plenty of head-room without micro-optimisation while keeping arithmetic identical to Python ints.
- Composite index is `(client_id, platform, action)` not `(client_id, platform)` so the dashboard's "show me everything we did for client X on platform Y" view is index-only.

cards.description:

notes.content:
🤖 Task Completed

**What was implemented**:
- `apps/api/alembic/versions/0004_create_onboarding_events.py` — migration per PRD §4.3.
  - `client_id` is a **nullable** FK to `clients(id)` with `ON DELETE SET NULL`. The PandaDoc signing webhook is the trigger that *creates* the matching `clients` row, so the event arrives before the client exists; the orchestrator backfills `client_id` on the same event row as part of the post-signing fan-out.

  - **`UniqueConstraint("event_type", "external_id", name="uq_onboarding_events_event_external")`** — the idempotency key for webhook replays from PandaDoc / GHL / Stripe / etc. Postgres treats NULLs as distinct under UNIQUE, so synthetic events with NULL external_id never collide with each other.

- `alembic upgrade head` (0003 → 0004) — clean.
- `alembic downgrade 0003_create_client_knowledge` — clean.
- `alembic upgrade head` re-applied — clean.

  - ✅ `test_duplicate_event_type_external_id_is_rejected` — second insert with same `(event_type='pandadoc.signed', external_id='doc_duplicate')` raises `IntegrityError`. This is what guarantees idempotent webhook retries — the orchestrator can replay the same PandaDoc event repeatedly without creating duplicate fan-outs.

- `client_id` FK has `ON DELETE SET NULL` (not `RESTRICT` or `CASCADE`). Retaining the audit trail is more valuable than referential integrity strictness; once an event happened, its existence is durable evidence even if the client row later gets purged.

cards.description:

**Tests**: Migration up/down. Insert with valid embedding succeeds. GIN index used by query planner for `value @>` lookup (verified via `EXPLAIN`).

notes.content:
🤖 Task Completed

**What was implemented**:
- `apps/api/alembic/versions/0003_create_client_knowledge.py` — Alembic migration creating the `client_knowledge` table per PRD §4.2.
  - `client_knowledge_source` ENUM with the six PRD values (`sales_call`, `agreement`, `portal`, `research`, `kickoff`, `manual`), declared once with `create_type=False` then reused as the column type (pattern from S1-06).
  - `embedding vector(1536)` column. Declared via an inline `UserDefinedType` subclass (`_Vector(1536)`) inside the migration so no `pgvector` Python dependency is required to run Alembic. Real reads/writes against vector data land in S1-30 onwards; the SDK will be added then.
  - `value` is `jsonb` with a GIN `jsonb_path_ops` index — more compact than the default GIN opclass and the right choice when only `@>` containment queries are needed (which is what the dashboard's knowledge-profile lookup does).
  - ivfflat index on `embedding` with `vector_cosine_ops` and `lists=100`. Default `lists` value tuned for the row counts we expect through Sprint 4; can be re-tuned later if needed.
  - `client_id` FK to `clients(id)` has `ON DELETE CASCADE` — wiping a client purges its full knowledge profile.
  - `captured_by` is a plain nullable UUID *without* an FK constraint. The FK to `users(id)` is added at the end of `0006_create_remaining_tables` (S1-10) once the users table exists. Documented inline in the migration so the deferred constraint is discoverable.
- `apps/api/tests/test_client_knowledge_table.py` (new) — 4 `@pytest.mark.db` tests.

**Verification (all green, 18/05/2026, against Neon staging)**:
- `alembic upgrade head` (0002 → 0003) — clean.
- `\d client_knowledge` confirms 9 columns plus the GIN + ivfflat indexes — 6 indexes total counting the PK.
- `alembic downgrade 0002_create_clients` — drops `client_knowledge` and the `client_knowledge_source` enum cleanly.
- `alembic upgrade head` re-applied — clean round-trip.
- `pytest tests/test_client_knowledge_table.py -v`:
  - ✅ `test_gin_index_on_value_exists` — checks `pg_indexes` for `using gin (value jsonb_path_ops)`.
  - ✅ `test_ivfflat_index_on_embedding_exists` — checks for `using ivfflat (embedding vector_cosine_ops)`.
  - ✅ `test_insert_with_valid_embedding_succeeds` — round-trips a 1536-dim zero vector via `cast(:vec AS vector(1536))` and confirms `embedding IS NOT NULL`.
  - ✅ `test_invalid_source_enum_is_rejected` — Postgres rejects `'NOT_A_SOURCE'`.

**Decisions**:
- Inline `UserDefinedType` over the `pgvector` package. Keeps the dep graph minimal for the schema work; switch to `pgvector.sqlalchemy.Vector` when the first query-side code lands.
- `jsonb_path_ops` GIN opclass over the default. Smaller index, faster `@>` lookups. Trade-off: only `@>` is supported (not `?` / `?&` / `?|` key-existence). Acceptable for the dashboard's knowledge-profile UI which only ever does containment.
- `ON DELETE CASCADE` on `client_id`. Knowledge profile rows are inseparable from their parent client; orphaning them would be a bug.

**Discovery captured in CHANGELOG**:
- SQLAlchemy `text()` bind-param parsing breaks on `:name::pg_type(N)` because the double-colon Postgres cast collides with the `:` bind marker. Workaround established: use `cast(:name AS pg_type(N))` SQL-standard form. Adopted as the project convention for type-casted parameters.

notes.content:
🤖 Task Completed

**What was implemented**:
- `apps/api/alembic/versions/0002_create_clients.py` — Alembic migration creating the `clients` table per PRD §4.1.
  - Two postgresql ENUM types: `campaign_flow_type` (2 values) and `current_step` (7 values), declared once with `create_type=False` and reused as the column type so SQLAlchemy emits the `CREATE TYPE` exactly once.
  - 22 base columns: id/email/business/contact/legal/phone/tier/fee + 2 enums + step_entered_at + parent_client_id self-FK + created_at/updated_at, plus 15 platform-ID text columns (`hubspot_contact_id` through `slack_thread_ts`).
  - `id` PK defaults to `gen_random_uuid()` (Postgres 13+ built-in - available on Neon PG 16.12 without `pgcrypto`).
  - `email` is `citext` so future returning-client lookups are case-insensitive without per-query lower(). Not UNIQUE (returning-client second-site rows share the email; linked via `parent_client_id`).
  - `parent_client_id` self-FK has `ON DELETE SET NULL` so deleting an old client row does not cascade-orphan its linked second-site row.
  - Indexes: `ix_clients_email`, `ix_clients_current_step`, `ix_clients_created_at_desc` (functional index with `DESC`), `ix_clients_parent_client_id`.
  - Downgrade reverses: drop indexes → drop table → drop both enum types (in that order so column references release first).
- `apps/api/tests/test_clients_table.py` (new) — 4 `@pytest.mark.db` tests covering the PRD contract.

**Verification (all green, 18/05/2026, against Neon staging)**:
- `alembic upgrade head` (`0001_create_extensions` → `0002_create_clients`) — clean.
- `alembic downgrade 0001_create_extensions` — clean. `\dt` confirms only `alembic_version` left. `SELECT typname FROM pg_type WHERE typtype='e'` returns 0 rows.
- `alembic upgrade head` re-applied — clean, idempotent round-trip.
- `pytest tests/test_clients_table.py -v` — 4 passed in 21.47s:
  - ✅ Insert with `legal_entity='UK'`, `current_step='sales_call'` succeeds (PK auto-generated via `gen_random_uuid()`).
  - ✅ Insert with `current_step='NOT_A_REAL_STEP'` raises `DBAPIError` (Postgres enum rejects unknown label).
  - ✅ Self-FK accepts a parent_id that exists (round-tripped via RETURNING).
  - ✅ Self-FK rejects a random UUID that has no matching row.
- `ruff check src tests alembic` — clean.

**Decisions**:
- `parent_client_id` uses `ON DELETE SET NULL` rather than `RESTRICT` or `CASCADE`. SET NULL preserves the child onboarding's history while letting an old archived parent be deleted; CASCADE would silently lose the second-site row.
- Platform ID columns stay plain `TEXT` (not per-platform CHECK constraints or sub-enums). Keeps the option to swap a platform out later without a migration; integrity is enforced by the writer code in S1-22 onwards rather than at column level.
- `gen_random_uuid()` rather than `uuid_generate_v4()`. The former is core Postgres 13+; the latter requires `uuid-ossp`. One fewer extension to enable across Neon prod / staging / per-PR branches (S1-33).

**Pattern established for later migrations (S1-07 → S1-10)**:
- Build the `postgresql.ENUM(..., create_type=False)` instance once per enum.
- Call `.create(bind, checkfirst=False)` explicitly at the top of `upgrade()`.
- Reuse the same instance as the column type in `op.create_table()`.
- In `downgrade()`, drop the table first, then `postgresql.ENUM(name="...").drop(bind, checkfirst=False)` for each enum.
This avoids the duplicate `CREATE TYPE` that occurs when generic `sa.Enum(name=..., create_type=False)` is used instead — see CHANGELOG Discovery entry for details.

**Deferred / next-up**:
- `client_knowledge.captured_by` FK to `users(id)` — users table doesn't exist until S1-10. S1-07 will declare the column as a nullable UUID without a FK constraint; the FK is added as part of S1-10 (`ALTER TABLE client_knowledge ADD CONSTRAINT ...`).

cards.title: 🔴 S1-05a: Strip libpq-only query params before asyncpg (Neon URL compat)
cards.description:
**Description**: `bullet_api.config.get_async_database_url()` rewrites the URL scheme from `postgresql://` to `postgresql+asyncpg://` but passes the query string through unchanged. Neon's canonical URL ships with `?sslmode=require&channel_binding=require` — these are libpq-only params; asyncpg rejects them at connect time with `TypeError: connect() got an unexpected keyword argument 'sslmode'`. As a result, `alembic upgrade head` (and any FastAPI/worker code path that opens an asyncpg pool) fails immediately against any Neon URL.

Fix scope:
- Strip `sslmode`, `channel_binding`, and any other libpq-only query params from the URL before returning from `get_async_database_url()`. Whitelist asyncpg-compatible params if any are present.
- Configure SSL via asyncpg's `connect_args={"ssl": ...}` on the SQLAlchemy engine (`apps/api/src/bullet_api/db/session.py`) so TLS is still enforced. Neon requires TLS, so `ssl=True` (or a context with `verify_mode=CERT_REQUIRED` and certifi roots) is the minimum.
- Keep `psql` and `scripts/verify_pgvector.py` working off the same canonical `DATABASE_URL` (those tools speak libpq and need the original query params). Only the asyncpg-bound copy is mutated; the original env var stays canonical.

Blocks: S1-04 (cannot deploy `bullet-api-staging` against `bullet-staging-env` without this fix — service crashes at startup).

**Tests**:
- New unit test for `get_async_database_url()`: input `postgresql://u:p@h/db?sslmode=require&channel_binding=require` returns `postgresql+asyncpg://u:p@h/db` (or an asyncpg-safe equivalent), no `sslmode` / `channel_binding` in the output URL.
- `alembic upgrade head` against `STAGING_DATABASE_URL_DIRECT` (from local `.env.neon`) completes without `TypeError`.
- Pytest DB smoke (`@pytest.mark.db`) passes when `DATABASE_URL` points at `STAGING_DATABASE_URL_POOLED`.
- TLS still enforced: a tampered ssl=disable connection should fail (negative assertion).

**Dependencies**: S1-03 (Neon projects must exist — already done; URLs captured in local `.env.neon`).

**Discovery context**: surfaced 18/05/2026 during S1-03 acceptance work. See `docs/CHANGELOG.md` 18/05/2026 entry + completion note on the S1-03 card. Worked around at the time by running `CREATE EXTENSION` via `psql` directly; Alembic path remains broken until this card lands.

notes.content:
🤖 Task Completed

**What was implemented**:
- `apps/api/src/bullet_api/config.py` — added `_strip_libpq_query_params()` plus a `_LIBPQ_ONLY_QUERY_PARAMS` deny-list covering `sslmode`, `channel_binding`, `sslrootcert`, `sslcert`, `sslkey`, `sslpassword`, `sslcrl`, `sslcrldir`, `sslcompression`, `gssencmode`, `krbsrvname`, `gsslib`. `get_async_database_url()` now performs both the scheme rewrite (`postgresql://` → `postgresql+asyncpg://`) and the query-string scrub in one pass.
